scope: Static source review of prepared ML-DSA-44 arithmetic, cache format, runtime wrappers and compiler binding; not overall release approval.
verdict: No blocking source defect found in the pinned files.

upstream.comparison: Local crates.io registry extraction compared byte-for-byte with vendored directory.

cacheFormat.representation: Immutable protected managed Blob; explicit signed i32 little-endian coefficients; no native struct layout, padding, pointers or alignment assumptions.
cacheFormat.arrayOrder: Key vectors: polynomial then coefficient. Matrix: row r then column s then coefficient; ExpandA samples rho || s || r.
cacheFormat.domains: A_hat retains upstream ordinary NTT coefficients; key polynomial fields retain upstream Montgomery representation. Reader uses i32::from_le_bytes without normalization.
cacheFormat.decoderTrust: Fixed cache lengths and coefficient invariants come from the matching factory and SDK protected-type provenance; arbitrary cache import is not allowed.

conclusions: Key generation retains its original key-pair return and local matrix scope. Only prepared construction requests a copy into an initialized matrix output; public preparation expands the canonical raw key and matrix once.

Signing and verification substitute only the supplied matrix. NTT/arithmetic/hashing/encodings modules are byte-identical to upstream; key/signature acceptance, hint checks, z norm and rejection sampling are unchanged.
Pure ML-DSA message/context framing, challenge hashes, signing rnd, masks and responses remain recomputed per call. ML-DSA-44 constants match upstream.
Runtime factories enforce raw key lengths and publish exactly initialized cache bytes only on success. Consumers validate context, signature and randomness lengths as applicable.

Compiler allocates outputs before forming borrowed payload pointers. Consumers create initialized temporary stack objects; no callback, GC safepoint, cache mutation or pointer retention occurs inside these runtime calls.
Upstream temporary key/polynomial Drop zeroization remains active. The retained managed secret cache is not securely erased by GC; no comprehensive scratch-erasure claim is made.
limitationsAndPendingGates: SDK nominal unforgeability and nonshared/nonstable enforcement are assumed; this source review does not prove the compiler/type-system boundary.

At the time of static review, executable vectors, interpreter/Wasm parity, GC retention, release Wasm stack bounds and measured performance approval were pending. Subsequent correctness/GC/stack evidence is linked below; performance remains a separate benchmark scope.

The optional output sink removed the source-level matrix return. Subsequent matrix-output-resolution.json confirms direct callers skip copying, and stack.json pins final frame bounds; instruction regression comparisons belong to the benchmark report.
Existing upstream unchecked u16 rejection-counter and incomplete raw-byte/SHAKE scratch-erasure limitations are not changed by this patch.

keyGenerationRevisionReview.directPath: key_gen_internal passes None, returns the original (PublicKey, PrivateKey), and executes the upstream arithmetic unchanged. No matrix is returned in the tuple.
keyGenerationRevisionReview.preparedPath: prepare_secret initializes all 16 matrix polynomials to zero, passes Some(&mut matrix), and clone_from overwrites every coefficient before serialization. All 28,800 cache bytes remain initialized.
keyGenerationRevisionReview.dropBehavior: The local generated matrix is dropped at its original upstream block boundary. The optional cloned matrix owns separate polynomial arrays; dropping the source cannot erase the destination. Public/secret key temporaries and prepared matrix retain their existing Drop behavior.
keyGenerationRevisionReview.branch: The added branch depends solely on the caller choosing None or Some; no new key-, message- or randomness-dependent decision is introduced.
keyGenerationRevisionReview.otherReviewedChange: Compiler register.ml now selects specialization.C.argument_types instead of specialization.P.argument_types; operand order, allocation-before-pointer formation and protected unwrap/wrap behavior are unchanged.
keyGenerationRevisionReview.executionAndStackStatus: Source review alone did not establish generated code behavior. Subsequent validation.json, stack.json and matrix-output-resolution.json record executed and Wasm evidence.
